description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Milner-Barry Gambit. Develop with 7...Nge7! and refuse the second pawn.

drills.briefExplanation: 6...cxd4 7.O-O Nge7! 8.Re1 Nf5 — take, then develop; don't grab the second pawn.
drills.description: Black to play. White plays 6.Bd3 — take on d4 and meet 7.O-O with 7...Nge7!.
drills.explanation: The safe defense: after 6...cxd4 7.O-O, Black develops with 7...Nge7! — refusing the greedy 7...dxc3?!. After 8.Re1 Nf5 Black's knight heads for its best square, the king will castle, and White's 'sacrifice' bought nothing: Black is a pawn up with a solid French structure. Develop first, grab later.
drills.name: Refusing the Pawn

drills.briefExplanation: 6...Nge7! 7.O-O Nf5 8.Re1 Be7 — develop everything before touching the center.
drills.description: Black to play. White develops 6.Bd3 — skip the capture and develop at once.
drills.explanation: The ultra-solid approach: Black doesn't even take on d4, playing 6...Nge7! at once. After 7.O-O Nf5 8.Re1 Be7 Black completes development with zero weaknesses — White's gambit idea never gets its trigger, the French structure is rock solid, and Black can later strike with ...f6. Sometimes the best counter to a gambit is ignoring it.
drills.name: Ignoring the Gambit
